items.subject: hss
items.title: Rules and why we have them
items.summary: Rules keep us safe and help us get along at home and school. Fair rules apply to everyone, and good helpers follow them.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Being a good citizen
items.summary: A good citizen is kind, tells the truth, shares, takes turns and takes care of things. We all belong to a group like a class or a family.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Symbols of our country
items.summary: The American flag, the Pledge of Allegiance and the bald eagle are symbols of the United States. Symbols stand for ideas we share.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Where am I? Near and far
items.summary: A map is a picture of a place from above. Words like near, far, left, right, up and down tell us where things are.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Maps and globes
items.summary: A globe is a round model of Earth, and a map is flat. Both show land and water and help us find places.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Jobs people do
items.summary: People work at jobs to earn money, and each job helps others. Doctors, farmers, teachers and builders all have important work.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Wants and needs
items.summary: Needs are things we must have, like food, water and shelter. Wants are extras that are nice to have, like toys.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Then and now
items.summary: Long ago, people lived and worked differently from today. We can compare then and now by looking at old and new tools, homes and clothes.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Holidays and traditions
items.summary: Holidays and traditions help families and communities remember people and events. Different families celebrate in different ways.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Stories of great Americans
items.summary: We learn from stories of people like Washington, Lincoln and Martin Luther King Jr. who did brave and helpful things.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Time words
items.summary: These words help us tell about time and order.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Community words
items.summary: These words help us talk about rules and living together.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Map words
items.summary: These words help us read maps and talk about places.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Fun fact: old and new tools
items.summary: Long ago, people washed clothes by hand and wrote with pens made from feathers. Today we have washing machines and computers.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Rules and laws
items.summary: Rules and laws keep people safe and settle problems fairly. Leaders and citizens each have jobs to help make and follow them.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Rights and responsibilities
items.summary: Citizens have rights, like speaking up, and responsibilities, like helping others and following laws.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Symbols and landmarks
items.summary: The flag, the Statue of Liberty and the Liberty Bell stand for ideas like freedom. Landmarks are well-known places that tell about our history.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Maps, globes and directions
items.summary: Maps use symbols and a key. The directions north, south, east and west help us find places on a map or globe.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Where we live
items.summary: Our address tells where we live, in a neighborhood, city, state and country. Land and weather affect how people live.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Places around the world
items.summary: People live in many places around the world, such as mountains, deserts and cities. Their homes, clothes and food fit the place.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Goods and services
items.summary: Goods are things people make or grow, and services are jobs people do for others. People trade money for both.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Producers and consumers
items.summary: Producers make goods or give services. Consumers buy and use them.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Families then and now
items.summary: Families long ago did chores and played differently. Looking at photos, tools and stories shows how family life has changed.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Holidays and traditions
items.summary: Families celebrate traditions in many ways. Some holidays remember important people or events in our country's past.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Everyday life in the past
items.summary: Long ago, people cooked, traveled and talked without cars, phones or computers. Inventions changed daily life.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Geography words
items.summary: Words for talking about places and maps.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Civics words
items.summary: Words about rules, leaders and being a citizen.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Fun fact: earning and saving
items.summary: People earn money by working. They can spend it on things they need, or save some for later.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Rules and laws, fairness
items.summary: Communities make laws so people stay safe and are treated fairly. Leaders like mayors help carry them out.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Government and leaders
items.summary: Governments make laws and provide services like schools, parks and fire stations. Citizens help by voting and being involved.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Local geography
items.summary: Our community has land, water and built places. Maps of our town show streets, parks and landmarks.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Where people came from
items.summary: People in our country came from many places around the world. They brought food, music, languages and traditions.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Work and trade
items.summary: People in different jobs depend on each other. We trade goods and services, and money makes trading easier.

items.subject: hss
items.title: How people make a difference
items.summary: One person can help change a community by being brave, kind or creative. Leaders, inventors and helpers have all done this.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Long-ago people and heroes
items.summary: People like Martin Luther King Jr. and Sally Ride did brave and important things. We can learn from their stories.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Immigrants and newcomers
items.summary: Immigrants are people who move to a new country. Many came to the United States to find safety, work or freedom.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Past, present and future
items.summary: History is the story of what happened in the past. A timeline puts events in order.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Cultures and traditions
items.summary: People in a community may speak different languages and celebrate different holidays. Sharing makes a community richer.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Historical sources
items.summary: We learn about the past from photos, letters, tools, maps and from asking older people about their lives.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Community words
items.summary: Words about government and living together.

items.subject: hss
items.title: History words
items.summary: Words used to talk about the past.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Fun fact: voting
items.summary: In a vote, people choose a leader or decide something together. Most adult citizens in the United States are allowed to vote.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Our local community
items.summary: Our community has its own geography and history. We can study it with maps, photos and stories.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Landmarks and regions
items.summary: Landmarks, rivers, mountains and cities help define a place. Regions are areas that share features such as climate.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Native peoples of the local region
items.summary: Native American peoples were the first people in most communities. Many nations still live here, and their cultures are still strong.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Explorers and settlers
items.summary: Explorers and settlers came from other places. They changed communities, and not everyone was treated fairly.

items.subject: hss
items.title: How communities change
items.summary: Towns grow and change over time because of people, new inventions and the land. Some things stay the same.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Immigration and a diverse community
items.summary: People from many countries have helped build our communities. Their food, music, languages and customs are part of our local culture.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Local government
items.summary: City and county governments make rules, run services and are led by elected people such as mayors and council members.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Constitution and citizens
items.summary: The Constitution is the plan for our government. Citizens have rights and also responsibilities, like obeying laws and voting.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Symbols of freedom
items.summary: The flag, the Pledge, the Liberty Bell and the Statue of Liberty are national symbols of freedom.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Local economy
items.summary: People in a community make and sell goods and services. Farms, shops and factories all play a part, and people trade across places.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Geography words
items.summary: Words about place and region.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Civics words
items.summary: Words about government and citizens.

items.subject: hss
items.title: History words
items.summary: Words for change over time.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Fun fact: continuity and change
items.summary: Some things in a town stay the same for hundreds of years, like a river or a festival. Other things, like buildings and jobs, change.

items.subject: hss
items.title: California geography
items.summary: California has coasts, mountains, valleys and deserts. Where people live and work depends on these regions.

items.subject: hss
items.title: California Native peoples
items.summary: Many Native nations lived in California for thousands of years and still do. They used land and resources wisely.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Exploration and missions
items.summary: Spanish explorers and missions changed life in California, especially for Native peoples. People today see this history from several points of view.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Ranchos and Mexican California
items.summary: After Mexico became independent, large ranches called ranchos shaped California life. Cattle hides and tallow were traded.

items.subject: hss
items.title: The Gold Rush
items.summary: Gold found in 1848 brought many people from across the world to California. The Gold Rush changed the land and the people living here.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Statehood
items.summary: California became a state in 1850. The state's growth brought new communities, laws and conflicts.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Railroads and growth
items.summary: The transcontinental railroad linked California to the east. Workers, including many Chinese immigrants, built it.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Water, farms and cities
items.summary: Farms, cities and industries grew as people built dams, canals and aqueducts to move water. California became a leader in farming and technology.

items.subject: hss
items.title: California government
items.summary: California's government has three branches. The state capital is Sacramento, and the state constitution sets the rules.

items.subject: hss
items.title: California's economy today
items.summary: California's economy includes farming, entertainment, technology and trade. Ports and highways help move goods.

items.subject: hss
items.title: California words
items.summary: Words for talking about California.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Fun fact: Sacramento
items.summary: Sacramento became California's capital in 1854. It sits where the American and Sacramento Rivers meet.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Geography of North America
items.summary: North America has varied lands and waters. Mountains, rivers and climate shaped where early peoples lived.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Early Native American nations
items.summary: Native nations across North America had many ways of life based on their lands. Many nations still thrive today.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Exploration and trade
items.summary: European explorers sought new routes and riches. Contact changed life for Native peoples, including through trade and disease.

items.subject: hss
items.title: The thirteen colonies
items.summary: Colonies grew along the Atlantic coast in New England, the Middle and the Southern regions. Each had its own economy and way of life.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Slavery in the colonies
items.summary: Enslaved Africans were forced to work in the colonies. Their labor and resistance are a central part of American history.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Causes of the American Revolution
items.summary: Colonists were angry about taxes and about having no say in British rule. Protests like the Boston Tea Party led to war.

items.subject: hss
items.title: The Declaration of Independence
items.summary: In 1776 the Declaration of Independence said people have rights, including life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. Thomas Jefferson wrote most of it.

items.subject: hss
items.title: The Revolutionary War
items.summary: The colonists fought Britain for independence, led by George Washington. They won, and the United States became a new country.

items.subject: hss
items.title: The Constitution
items.summary: The Constitution set up our government with three branches and checks and balances. The Bill of Rights protects basic freedoms.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Westward expansion
items.summary: After the Revolution, settlers moved west. This growth affected Native peoples and led to new states.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Regions of the United States
items.summary: The United States has regions like the Northeast, South, Midwest and West. Land and climate shape each region's work and life.

items.subject: hss
items.title: American history words
items.summary: Words about the colonies and the new nation.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Civics words
items.summary: Words about government and citizens.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Fun fact: Declaration date
items.summary: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776. We celebrate this day as Independence Day.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Early humans and the Neolithic revolution
items.summary: Early people moved from hunting and gathering to farming. This led to villages, tools and eventually cities.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Mesopotamia and Egypt
items.summary: Early civilizations grew along rivers like the Tigris, Euphrates and Nile. They developed writing, laws and cities.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Ancient Hebrews and Kush
items.summary: Ancient Hebrews formed a monotheistic religion that shaped later traditions. Kush was a powerful kingdom in Africa along the Nile.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Ancient India and China
items.summary: India's early civilizations gave us ideas in religion and math. China's dynasties built cities, a Great Wall and an empire.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Ancient Greece
items.summary: Greek city-states like Athens and Sparta had different ways of governing. Athens developed early democracy, and Greeks excelled in art, philosophy and science.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Ancient Rome
items.summary: Rome grew from a city into a huge republic and then an empire. Its law, roads and engineering shaped the Western world.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Geography of the ancient world
items.summary: Rivers, seas and deserts influenced where ancient people lived and traded. Maps help us follow their movements.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Ancient world words
items.summary: Words about early civilizations.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Fun fact: Alphabet origins
items.summary: Many writing systems began in the ancient world, and our alphabet traces back through Greece and Rome. Writing let people keep records and share ideas.

items.subject: hss
items.title: The fall of Rome and early Middle Ages
items.summary: After Rome's empire in the west ended, Europe had smaller kingdoms. Christianity and the Byzantine Empire helped carry ideas forward.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Islamic civilization
items.summary: Islam spread from Arabia and built a large civilization. Scholars made advances in science, medicine, math and art.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Medieval Africa and Asia
items.summary: West African kingdoms like Ghana, Mali and Songhai grew rich on trade. China, Japan and Korea had powerful states and fresh inventions.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Medieval Europe
items.summary: In medieval Europe, kings, lords and peasants lived under feudalism. Churches, castles and towns shaped daily life.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Americas before and after contact
items.summary: Mesoamerican and Andean peoples like the Maya, Aztec and Inca built large civilizations. European contact brought deep changes.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Renaissance and Reformation
items.summary: The Renaissance brought new art and learning. The Reformation changed Christianity and Europe.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Age of Exploration
items.summary: European ships crossed oceans in search of trade, land and wealth. Exploration led to new contacts and conflicts.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Medieval and early modern words
items.summary: Words about this era.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Fun fact: Printing press
items.summary: In the 1400s, Johannes Gutenberg's printing press made books cheaper and helped ideas spread quickly across Europe.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Ideas of the American founding
items.summary: The Revolution and the Constitution were built on ideas of liberty and self-government. Founders debated how much power each level of government should have.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Growth of a new nation
items.summary: In the early republic, the nation grew with new states, roads and canals. Political parties and public debates took shape.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Westward expansion
items.summary: The country grew by purchase and war, such as the Louisiana Purchase. Native nations were forced from their lands, and settlers had hard journeys.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Industrial revolution and reform
items.summary: Factories and new machines changed work and cities. Reform movements worked for causes like women's rights and ending slavery.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Slavery and the road to Civil War
items.summary: Slavery divided the nation. Disagreements over it, along with abolitionists' work, led to the Civil War.

items.subject: hss
items.title: The Civil War
items.summary: From 1861 to 1865, the Union and Confederacy fought. The war ended slavery and tested the United States.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Reconstruction
items.summary: After the war, the country tried to rebuild and protect the rights of formerly enslaved people. Constitutional amendments made big changes, but many rights were later denied.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Growth and Conflict words
items.summary: Words from this unit.

items.subject: hss
items.title: Fun fact: Emancipation Proclamation
items.summary: President Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863. It declared people held as slaves in rebelling states to be free.
